title: 20.7 Exercise and Rehabilitation of People with Diseases

cards.front: When did cardiopulmonary rehabilitation programs originate, and what is their status in clinical disease management?
cards.back: Cardiopulmonary rehabilitation programs began in the 1950s and have become the most visible and established clinical exercise rehabilitation programs.

cards.front: Which major professional association and research journal emerged from advances in cardiopulmonary rehabilitation?
cards.back:
Advances led to the formation of:
  • AACVPR: The American Association of Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Rehabilitation.
  • Official Journal: The Journal of Cardiopulmonary Rehabilitation and Prevention.

cards.front: For which major oncological and metabolic diseases is exercise an essential component of rehabilitation?
cards.back:
Exercise training is an essential component of clinical rehabilitation for:
  • Cancer: Counteracts disease- and treatment-related fatigue while preserving functional capacity.
  • Obesity: Facilitates weight management and metabolic health.
  • Diabetes: Enhances glycemic control and insulin sensitivity.

cards.front: Which renal and chronic pulmonary conditions benefit from exercise rehabilitation?
cards.back:
Structured exercise rehabilitation is an important component of management for:
  • Renal Disease: Improves functional physical capacity and stamina in kidney disease patients.
  • Cystic Fibrosis: Enhances ventilatory efficiency, airway clearance, and aerobic capacity.

cards.front: How does exercise rehabilitation benefit patients with musculoskeletal, joint, and chronic pain disorders?
cards.back:
Exercise rehabilitation is prescribed to maintain functional capacity and manage symptoms in:
  • Osteoporosis: Preserves bone mineral density and structural integrity.
  • Arthritis: Maintains joint range of motion and functional mobility.
  • Fatigue & Pain Syndromes: Improves exercise tolerance in chronic fatigue syndrome and fibromyalgia.

cards.front: What specific clinical benefit does exercise rehabilitation provide for organ transplant recipients?
cards.back: In recipients of heart, liver, or kidney transplants, exercise rehabilitation is emphasized because it directly helps alleviate pharmacological drug side effects (such as immunosuppressive-induced muscle wasting) and improves overall general health.

cards.front: What is the relationship between specific physiological mechanisms and general health benefits in disease rehabilitation?
cards.back: Although the specific physiological mechanisms explaining exercise benefits for each disease have not been fully defined, exercise training imparts broad general health benefits that significantly improve patient prognosis and functional status.

cards.front: Why must exercise programming in disease rehabilitation be highly individualized?
cards.back: The application of exercise in rehabilitation is highly specific to the nature and extent of the individual disease, requiring customized exercise prescriptions tailored to the patient's specific clinical status and pathology.
